title: How to Make Someone Sit in Smoke
request: Tape 01 again, in plain words. Biku found the first script weird and random, like broken English; Claude rewrote the same story in full plain sentences and he said yes, do it. Vertical.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: If a room filled with smoke, would you get up and *leave?*

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: You think you would. Watch this.
lines.say: You think you would... Watch this.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: This man came here to earn twenty dollars. All he has to do is sit and wait.

lines.speaker: copycat
lines.text: Twenty dollars just to sit here? *Easy.*
lines.say: Twenty dollars, just to sit here? Easy.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: What he does not know is that everyone else in this room *works for me.*
lines.say: What he does not know, is that everyone else in this room... works for me.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: I pay them to do one thing. Stay *calm,* whatever happens.
lines.say: I pay them to do one thing. Stay calm... whatever happens.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: Now I let *smoke* into the room.
lines.say: Now... I let smoke into the room.

lines.speaker: copycat
lines.text: Is that smoke?
lines.say: Is that... smoke?

lines.speaker: cheat
lines.text: It's nothing. Probably the kitchen.

lines.speaker: copycat
lines.text: Nobody else looks worried. So it must be fine.
lines.say: Nobody else looks worried... So, it must be fine.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: See what he did? He did not look at the smoke. He looked at *the people.*
lines.say: See what he did? He did not look at the smoke. He looked... at the people.

lines.speaker: copycat
lines.text: It's getting hard to breathe. Shouldn't we tell someone?
lines.say: It's getting hard to breathe... Shouldn't we tell someone?

lines.speaker: cheat
lines.text: Relax. If it was dangerous, somebody would say so.

lines.speaker: copycat
lines.text: Yeah. You're right. It's *fine.*
lines.say: Yeah... You're right. It's fine.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: Now he has said it is fine. Leaving would mean admitting he was *wrong.*
lines.say: Now, he has said it is fine. Leaving would mean admitting... he was wrong.

lines.speaker: copycat
lines.text: My eyes are burning. Is nobody going to move?
lines.say: My eyes are burning! Is nobody going to move?

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: What do you think he *does?*
lines.say: What do you think... he does?

lines.speaker: copycat
lines.text: They are all calm. I must be the one who is *wrong.*
lines.say: They are all calm... I must be the one, who is wrong.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: He *stays.*

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: This is not a story. In 1968, two scientists did this *for real.*
lines.say: This is not a story. In 1968, two scientists did this... for real.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: Alone in the smoke, three people out of four got up and reported it.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: With two calm strangers beside them, only *one in ten* did.
lines.say: With two calm strangers beside them... only one in ten did.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: The smoke was the same. Only the faces changed.
lines.say: The smoke was the same. Only the faces... changed.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: You do this too. A fire alarm rings, everyone looks around, and nobody moves first.
lines.say: You do this too. A fire alarm rings, everyone looks around... and nobody moves first.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Here is how you beat it. When something feels wrong, do not check the faces around you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They are checking yours. Say it out loud, and *stand up first.*
lines.say: They are checking yours. Say it out loud... and stand up first.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: One person standing up breaks the whole trick.
lines.say: One person standing up, breaks the whole trick.

lines.speaker: trainer
lines.text: So how long would you sit in smoke? As long as everyone else does.
lines.say: So, how long would you sit in smoke? As long... as everyone else does.

sources: Bibb Latané and John M. Darley, Group inhibition of bystander intervention in emergencies, Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 1968, volume 10, number 3, pages 215 to 221, https://doi.org/10.1037/h0026570 : people filling in a questionnaire while smoke came into the room. Alone, 75% reported the smoke within the six minutes (three out of four); with two others who had been told to stay passive, 10% did (1 of 10); in groups of three real participants, someone reported it in 38% of groups. Fairly sure: the figures were checked on 2026-10-12 against several summaries of the paper that agree with each other and with the citation (a NIST record gives the same journal, volume and pages); the paper itself was not opened. What the scene invents: the twenty dollars, the Trainer, the room, the Cheat and the row of four. The study had a questionnaire, a vent and two calm actors.
